input.title: ZM3D playable - brief for PlayableX
input.bodyText:
ZM3D playable - brief for PlayableX
Zombie Match 3D (store name: Puzzles vs Zombies). Brief owner: Julia Lawson. Written 1 Oct 2025 for the game as it plays today. We are looking at a change to the core gameplay. If it goes ahead, we'll redo the parts it touches with you in November.

1. Start date
Project kickoff: Monday 3 November 2025 (call booked 17:00-17:30 UTC). Whatever we still owe you is tracked line by line in the hand-off list (link at the end).

2. Scenario and what it is for
We picked Scenario 1, the core game mechanic, shown simply. The playable is there to filter for retention: players who don't enjoy the real game should drop out at the ad, and the ones who install should already know what they're getting. So it has to stay true to the core gameplay. It isn't a fun casual ad unrelated to the game. Unlike the Domino Delights playable, it shouldn't feel like it's on rails: the player can pick any items on the board and keep making matches for as long as they're good enough to.

3. How a level plays
- Items sit in a 3D physics pile. They settle and cover each other, so digging uncovers buried matches.
- The player drags items into a tray with 7 slots.
- Three matching items in the tray clear, and the match fires that item at the zombies coming in (the cannon / rocket launcher with its projectile). Each item hits differently: for example, the grenade is powerful, the couch does splash damage, and the plushie is weak but funny.
- If all 7 slots fill without a match, that's a blunder. The tray clears and the surviving zombies enrage, but play carries on. A blunder slows the player down; it doesn't end the level.
- Win: every zombie on screen is eliminated.
- Lose: the zombies reach the player and the player's HP runs out. The loss screen only appears at zero HP.
Reference: the reference-level deck (ZM3D playable - reference level) and the recording Brian sent you on 24 Sep show the level we built for you.

4. The board: eight default items
Grenade, Couch and Plushie Chick (the three from the reference level; the chick is the "duck" you asked about), plus Shuriken, Cute Axe, Gift Box, Cactus Plant and Dynamite.
Every other board item on the pack list is an extra you can swap in on the editable board. In the hand-off list, the Board set column shows Default for the eight and Extra for the rest.
Also used: the Cannon (rocket launcher, with its projectile) and the background from the reference level.

5. Zombies and animation
Four zombies: Party Girl, Plumber, Magician, Football Player.
One animation: walk.
All four are in the Unity package Brian sent on 26 Sep, which you're re-rigging in Spine. We can talk about more zombies later if scope and file size allow.

6. Sound and music
You can use: Matching, Success and Failure sounds (made in-house, already in the outgoing folder). The background music will be a track made in-house just for the ad, not the in-game track. It's still being cut down to a loop and will follow.
Still to come: the Rocket and Explosion sounds currently in the game come from a sound library and a bought pack, so we can't hand them over. We'll send our own versions once they're made.
Music: as you told us on the Domino playable, the music only starts after the player's first tap. Nothing plays before that.

7. File formats (from your list, unchanged)
- 3D: .fbx (Binary, not ASCII), .glb or .blend
- 2D: .png (character parts split into pieces for 2D animation)
- Font: .ttf or .woff2
- Sound: .mp3 or .wav

8. What's still coming from us
See "ZM3D playable - hand-off list". It has one row per line of Brian's pack list, each marked Delivered (you have the current file), Ready (exported, current, waiting in our outgoing folder) or Owed (with what's owed and who has it). As of 1 Oct: 8 Delivered, 48 Ready, 40 Owed. Seven of the eight default board items are Delivered or Ready. The Cactus Plant is getting a new colour version and will follow.

Done. Both files are in my Drive, shared view-only with everyone on the Nov 3 kickoff hold and with PlayableX's intake address.
• Brief: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1f4481f99e61d8ef01cf7e28/edit
• Hand-off list: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1n2cSQsrN36W3toYhKsSkXc4QLa_WaaBIgaWZ9r10vv8/edit

Counts across the 96 lines of Brian's pack list:
• *Delivered: 8* (the first zip, the chick, and the zombie Unity pack)
• *Ready: 48*
• *Owed: 40*. Of those, 21 are with Claire, 18 with Brian, 3 with Calvin and 1 with Martin

Since Brian wrote his notes, a few lines went back to Owed:
• Claire is redoing the bathroom UVs, so the 12 bathroom files from Fri 26 Sep are the old version
• Robert made new colour versions of the Cactus, Chainsaw and Cone after they were exported. The Cactus is one of the default eight, and it's the only one of the eight that isn't Delivered or Ready
• The instruments zip got cut off on upload, so those 8 aren't in the outgoing folder
• The Rocket and Explosion sounds come from a library and a bought pack, so they stay with us until Calvin makes our own versions

Robert's picks haven't changed. All 40 Owed tickets are in Todo, each with a comment saying what's owed and who has it.

Hi <@PERSON_6078_SLACK_ID>, ahead of the Nov 3 start, here are the two documents for the Zombie Match 3D playable:
• *Brief* (what to build from: Scenario 1, the eight default board items, the four zombies with the walk animation, win/lose and the 7-slot tray, sound and when music can start, formats): https://docs.google.com/document/d/1f4481f99e61d8ef01cf7e28/edit
• *Hand-off list* (every line of the asset pack, marked Delivered, Ready or Owed): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1n2cSQsrN36W3toYhKsSkXc4QLa_WaaBIgaWZ9r10vv8/edit

Right now that's 8 delivered, 48 ready on our side, and 40 still coming from us. The Owed rows in the sheet list exactly what's still to come. Both are also shared with intake@playablex.ai. We wrote it for the game as it is today; if the core gameplay changes, we'll go through the affected parts with you in November.

Correction to the split: Brian has 15 Owed lines, not 18 (5 exports, the 8 instruments, item visuals and UI). So it's Claire 21, Brian 15, Calvin 3, Martin 1, for 40 in total. The sheet already has it right.
